summary: Adds an email search filter to the users index, a self-service profile update and a user destroy action. Also adds an after_save hook that sends a welcome email.

findings.title: Search term interpolated into SQL
findings.problem: The index action puts params[:q] straight into the SQL text of the where clause. Any authenticated user controls that text.
findings.consequence: An authenticated caller can inject SQL and read or change any row, including api_token and admin columns.
findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Destroy action exempted from admin check
findings.problem: The change adds destroy to the except list of require_admin. Any authenticated user can now call DELETE /users/:id on any id.
findings.consequence: Any user with a token can delete every other account, including admins.
findings.fix: Remove destroy from the except list so only admins can delete users.

findings.title: Profile update permits every attribute
findings.problem: The profile action permits all user params, so the caller can set any column on their own record. ApplicationController trusts the admin and api_token columns of that record for authorization.
findings.consequence: Any user can make themselves an admin or overwrite their api_token. That escalates to full admin access.
findings.fix: Permit only the fields a user may edit, such as email.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The after_save callback fires on every create and every update. Each profile edit and every other save queues a new welcome email.
findings.consequence: Users get repeated welcome emails whenever their record changes.
findings.fix: Use after_create_commit so the welcome email goes out once, after the record is committed.

findings.title: New actions have no covering test
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the search filter, profile, destroy or the welcome email callback. These add new branches and side effects.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization and filtering will go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add request tests for index search, profile and destroy, including the non-admin cases.
